title: Thermodynamics-Aware 2D Finite-Temperature PEPO
eyebrow: Harnessing Quantum 2026 · Challenge #147 · Deadline Technical Report
lede: We implemented a resumable, auditable 10×10 finite-temperature PEPO prototype pipeline and proposed a compression objective that directly preserves thermodynamic information under fixed tensor capacity. The current evidence establishes the representation, objective, checkpoints, and independent ED/QMC validation chain; the full β range and bond-dimension convergence benchmark remain incomplete.

sections.title: Physics Problem
sections.note: Near the critical field, growing correlations in low-temperature thermal states make 2D tensor-network compression genuinely difficult.

blocks.text: The target thermal operator is $R(\beta)=e^{-\beta H}$. A finite-temperature PEPO represents this exponentially large operator as a 2D tensor network. Imaginary-time evolution continually generates new correlations, while a fixed virtual bond dimension D forces the algorithm to decide which information to retain.

rows: Two PEPO points, one QMC point, and an ED curve

sections.title: Innovation Hypothesis
sections.note: The proposed innovation changes how information is allocated at finite D rather than simply increasing compute or bond dimension.

blocks.text: From approximating the full operator to prioritizing thermodynamics

Ordinary Frobenius compression asks whether the student is close to the teacher as a huge matrix. The thermodynamic objective additionally asks whether finite capacity preserves statistical weight, mean energy, and physical Hermiticity. The physical picture resembles observable-aware coarse graining: directions irrelevant to macroscopic thermodynamics may be sacrificed so that finite D is reserved for correlation channels that actually change f, u, and thermal response.

The loss protects z and u but does not directly protect C. If, at matched D, χ, Δβ, and optimization budget, thermodynamic PEPO reduces the QMC error in u and also improves the held-out C(β), that would indicate preservation of a consistent thermodynamic structure along imaginary-time evolution rather than fitting only two numbers.

blocks.label: Prediction awaiting validation
blocks.why: Testing it requires a matched ordinary chain, the full β curve, and QMC estimates of C(β).

sections.title: Algorithm and Data Flow
sections.note: Every step leaves a resumable scientific state that cannot be silently overwritten.

blocks.title: PEPO pipeline
items: Start from the identity PEPO at β=0.
Apply a second-order symmetric Trotter step to generate a temporary teacher, with target production limit D²=16.
Compress back to student D=4 under matched initialization, χ, cutoff, and optimization budget.
After checking finiteness, maximum bond dimension, positive partition function, and Hermiticity, atomically write an NPZ+JSON checkpoint.
Separate measurement from evolution so χ can vary independently without reoptimizing the PEPO.

blocks.label: Current probe budget
blocks.text: To obtain verifiable output within the supercomputing time limit, this PEPO probe set max_iterations=1. Both checkpoints retained the finite initial PEPO and accepted no optimization update. The probe therefore validates the representation and diagnostic pipeline, not an accuracy improvement caused by optimization.

sections.title: Results and Interpretation
sections.note: Each figure states both the supported conclusion and the boundary beyond which extrapolation is not justified.

items.caption: Partially established. The left panel overlays the 4×4 ED finite-size curve, two 10×10 thermodynamic-PEPO probe points, and the extrapolated 10×10 QMC point at β=0.5. The right panel contains only the 4×4 ED specific heat. The figure shows that outputs from independent methods can be assembled, but it is not a complete accuracy comparison at matched size and temperature range. The PEPO points β=0.025 and 0.05 lie outside the challenge target interval.

Internal consistency passed. At β=0.05, |Δu|=3.58×10⁻⁸ and |Δz|=6.09×10⁻¹⁰, with all objective components finite; β=0.025 is near machine precision. Because no ordinary production baseline exists and zero updates were accepted, this figure does not establish a method advantage. It only shows that the objective and diagnostics can be evaluated stably.

blocks.text: Figure 3 · QMC Trotter extrapolation and chain diagnostics

items.caption: Validation passed. The M=32, 64, and 128 data at βJ=0.5 were linearly extrapolated in (β/M)², yielding u∞/J=−2.90970±0.00299. Error bars are 8-bin block-bootstrap standard errors, and the green band is the zero-step 95% bootstrap confidence interval. The maximum R̂ is 1.0211<1.05 and the maximum split-half |z| is 1.7907<3.

The resource bottleneck is visible. The second imaginary-time step took about 59 minutes and peaked near 9.7 GiB, substantially more than the first step. Both checkpoints have zero Hermiticity residual and maximum bond dimension 4, but neither accepted an optimizer update. This supports engineering feasibility and enforcement of physical constraints, not low-temperature stability or convergence.

blocks.title: Traceability principles
items: Use only success/complete manifests and accepted analyses.
Each PEPO checkpoint simultaneously validates path β, mode, lattice, D, χ, and configuration SHA.
The ED table must match the manifest SHA-256 and state_count=65536.
Do not compute C from two PEPO points, interpolate missing β values, or treat 4×4 ED as 10×10 ground truth.
PNG files are 300 DPI; PDFs contain no embedded raster-image objects and remain vector outputs.

sections.title: Limitations and Risks
sections.note: The most important scientific risks are shown explicitly because they determine whether the next computation is worthwhile.

rows: The current thermodynamic objective did not actually change the student
First obtain a nonzero-update ordinary/thermodynamic ablation on a small system
Error differences cannot be attributed to the new objective
Match every budget parameter and change only the loss function
No data in the target β range
Low-temperature stability in the quantum-critical fan cannot be assessed
Advance checkpoints point by point to β≥0.1, then extend within budget
The D=4 result may be dominated by representation bias
Compare D=4, 6, and 8 at β=0.1 and 0.5
Contraction and Trotter errors may masquerade as method improvement
Vary χ and Δβ separately; do not merge the error sources
C requires differentiation or fluctuation estimation
Cross-check a dense β grid against QMC C

blocks.label: Key risk
blocks.why: Small teacher–student Δu/Δz does not automatically imply better agreement with QMC. Only a matched ordinary ablation and an independent QMC curve can validate the innovation.

sections.title: Why This Is Worth Continuing
sections.note: The research opportunity comes from a clear, falsifiable hypothesis that can be expanded step by step.

blocks.title: Near term: prove that the objective changes the representation
items: Obtain nonzero optimizer updates on 2×2 and 4×4 systems and compare with exact exp(−βH).
Fix D, χ, Δβ, initialization, and iteration budget, then complete matched ordinary and thermodynamic chains.
Evaluate u and z first, while reserving C as a held-out generalization metric.

blocks.title: Medium term: complete the core challenge evidence
items: Generate 10×10 f, u, and C over βJ∈[0.1,1.0].
Use QMC to report pointwise relative errors and the largest stable β.
Produce independent convergence plots for D=4, 6, 8 and for χ and Δβ.

blocks.title: Long term: establish a methodological contribution
items: Position observable-aware, free-energy-aware, and environment-aware compression within the literature.
Explore purification or positive-definite PEPO parameterizations that guarantee positivity rather than only Hermiticity.
Compare wall time, memory, and low-temperature reach against tanTRG at matched accuracy.
Transfer the method to frustrated magnets and correlated-electron models where the sign problem makes QMC unavailable.

blocks.label: Research potential
blocks.text: If the thermodynamic objective consistently improves the held-out C(β) at matched computational budget, it would be more than an engineering patch: it would become a generalizable answer to what physical information finite tensor capacity should preserve.
